title.narrative: Monitoring and Evaluation of Development Progress(2004-2006)

description.narrative: Institutional Development: China's statistical system is in transition. A vast amount of data is collected, but there are some gaps in coverage, while lags in the collection and processing of data constrain real time M&E on achievement of key development goals. The official agencies rely on a large number of indicators to track development programs and projects, but they are largely input indicators, rather than results-based measures that can be extracted from the existing statistical collection effort. Where outcomes are monitored, there is a need to bring the information together to develop a comprehensive and fairly continuous view of development progress that goes beyond measuring broad targets and physical achievements. Further, there is need to sharpen the focus to construct an effective, transparent and sustainable M&E system. Improving M&E at the Provincial Level. As agreed within the development community, the MDGs will function as a primary anchor for M&E efforts to measure progress towards development goals. While at an aggregate national level China has already met many MDG goals, this success masks shortfalls in lagging areas that have inadequate access to social services and poor social indicators. A set of regionally disaggregated MDG indicators is therefore needed, given China.s vast size and the new Government's focus on correcting geographical inequalities. While much of the effort will focus on developing such indicators, weaknesses in the national level indicators also need to be addressed.both the statistical definitions and collection effort (some addressed already under previous and existing ESW and TA), and the ability to marshal the statistical evidence into a formal review format and associate such reviews with program evaluations. The objective of the Grant is to assist the Recipient to develop a monitoring and evaluation framework for Five-Year Plans.
